subject.title: MEDIA: directive with absolute local paths outside default media roots silently fails (Telegram)

question: Should this issue be scoped to reason-specific diagnostics for blocked Telegram `MEDIA:` paths while https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/47002 owns configurable root expansion, or should this issue also define a new host-local media root contract?
rationale: The diagnostics half is a narrow media-delivery improvement, but accepting additional absolute host paths or adding a config escape hatch changes a public configuration and file-read/upload security boundary.

options.title: Diagnostics Here, Roots In Canonical Policy
options.body: Keep this issue focused on warn-level dropped-media reasons and optional safe user notice, while the configurable-root contract stays with https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/47002 or the approved `tools.fs.roots` design.

options.title: Make This The Root-Policy Item
options.body: Use this issue to define Telegram outbound media root configuration, accepting that it must cover schema, docs, migration/doctor expectations, and security review.

options.title: Document Current Boundary Only
options.body: Decline new root expansion and only document managed roots, supported staging directories, and the CLI workaround, leaving diagnostics as the only possible repair.

recommendation.title: Diagnostics Here, Roots In Canonical Policy
recommendation.body: Keep this issue focused on warn-level dropped-media reasons and optional safe user notice, while the configurable-root contract stays with https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/47002 or the approved `tools.fs.roots` design.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest recent history on the outbound media access policy and shared media plumbing involved in the decision.
